touch_pressure_scale.infant_acute_pain_threshold: UNMEASURED - the child algometry study excludes neonates
touch_pressure_scale.reading: The skin unit is anchored to sustained-ischaemia pressures, not to acute pain. TACTILE_PAIN_START 10,000 Pa is 18x below the measured acute pressure pain threshold in children (180,000 Pa) and 2.3x above capillary closing pressure (4,266 Pa). For an infant holding one posture, ischaemia is the mechanism that matters, so the magnitude is defensible and the NAME is not. The acute threshold for infants specifically is unmeasured: the child algometry study excludes neonates.

command_following.gauge: env.py cmd_response_slow, the net 250 ms comparison: cos = direction match of the rotation asked at the start of the hold against the rotation that had happened 25 ticks later (+1 exact, 0 sideways, -1 against); achieved share = their size ratio; rail = share of decoded controls at |1| during the hold
command_following.selection_rule: highest direction match with under 20% of controls on the rail, ties to the higher achieved share
command_following.unscored_rule: a trial whose gauge reading scored no part (n = 0) has no direction match: it is counted in trials_unscored and per_group_unscored and left out of every mean; until 2026-09-23 it was counted as a direction match of 0
command_following.closer_rule: closer_out_of_100: of 100 ordered parts, how many ended the hold nearer the ordered orientation than they began it (0 = none, 100 = every one); gap_closed_pct: the share of the ordered turn's degrees closed, summed over the cell's parts (0% = never moved, 100% = arrived; negative = ended farther away); position_match_mean is read only on trials that ordered a position step (the wrists); direction_match_ci95 = mean +- 1.96 standard errors
command_following.code: commit b55ee9a4d (the env gauge finds the eyes' row by name and scores each order over exactly its 25 ticks; the tool leaves out a trial the gauge scored no part for, 5beac622f) plus the tool's added readings committed with this entry (position read only on the wrist trials, parts ending nearer, share of the ordered turn closed, the 95% interval). Same seed and grid as the 2026-09-18 table, so the same orders. Scratch record: rowfix/lh84_cf_table.json (env.py blob da0f108c5, 924 s on the CPU).
command_following.reading: At H84's decoder gain 6 and half strength, one 20-degree order to one body part on physics alone turns 75% of the way from 'unrelated to the order' (0%) to 'exactly the ordered way' (100%), 95% interval 65% to 85%; 28 of 30 ordered parts (93 of every 100) end nearer the ordered orientation, and the parts close 35% of the ordered 20 degrees in 250 ms. The chest is scored in every cell (22% to 95% of the way; 2 trials per cell). The declared rule picks gain 6 at half strength again, but every one of the 20 cells has a 95% interval reaching 65%, so 30 trials per cell do not separate the gains.
command_following.compared_with_2026_09_18: The superseded table read 72% of the way for this cell: its 2 chest trials in 30 went in as 0 because the gauge never scored the chest (77% without them), it read ticks 26 and 27 of a 27-tick hold, and its position match counted the 26 of every 30 trials that order no position step as 0 (10% of the way in this cell; the wrist trials alone read 75% now).

following_out_of_100.question: When an order tells a body part to turn to a new orientation, is the part closer to that orientation 250 ms later (one order's tenure: 5 model steps x 5 physics ticks of 10 ms) than when the order was given? Counted per part per order; the eyes' row is left out (it is served by the eye servo, not by the joints).
following_out_of_100.scale: 0 of 100 = no part ever ends closer; 100 of 100 = every part always ends closer

physics_only_reachable_pose.what: no model: every part ordered back to a whole-body pose the same body reached 60 ticks earlier (median ordered turn 4.6 degrees), strength 0.5, decoder gain 6; the line for orders the body can carry out

physics_only_independent_random_turns.what: no model: every part ordered to turn 20 degrees about its own random axis at once, strength 0.5, decoder gain 6; orders that need not fit together

chance_order_ignored.what: the live parts' real 250 ms turns scored against 200 targets each at the same distance in random directions: the count reached when the turn ignores the order. It is not 50: a turn about as large as the distance lands closer to a random target about 1 time in 4

live_model_orders.what: the H84 segment 31 checkpoint ckpt_step_344400 acting in its own saved world (5 of the 8 saved bodies, 245 whole orders, learning off, CPU); median ordered turn 23.8 degrees, median turn made 13.7 degrees

following_out_of_100.reading: Live orders end closer 54 times in 100, against 31 when the order is ignored and 87 when physics alone carries out reachable orders; summed over all parts the distance to the ordered orientation grows 3.4% in 250 ms, because the parts that miss end farther away by more than the parts that hit gain.

vestibular_scales.meaning: each scale is the pooled 99th percentile of 18,450 env frames (15,000 motor babble, 2,400 placed on a side or face down, 600 torque rolls, 450 drops from 10 cm), rounded, so that percentile reads about 1 in the model's vestibular vector

scales.head_acc: 9.81 m/s2 = one g (fixed by the contract, not measured)

lived_ends.head_acc_norm_g: lying still 1.00; babbling on the back 2.40 (p99); a 10 cm drop onto the back 41.6 (one frame)
lived_ends.support_total_body_weights: lying still 1.00; babbling 1.01 (median) to 3.57 (p99); drop impact 18.3
lived_ends.gyro_on_scale: the vector's 1 on this field is 115 degrees per second of head turning (2.0 rad/s); lying still, 99 of 100 frames turn slower than 6 degrees per second; babbling, slower than 76 degrees per second; a roll, slower than 533 degrees per second, which the vector reads as 4.7 times its scale
